text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on August 22 in history:
1138 - The English defeated the Scots at Cowton Moor. Banners of various saints were carried into battle which led to it being called the Battle of the Standard.
1350 - Philip VI of France died and was succeeded by John II. He was reigning monarch at the outbreak of the Hundred Years War (1337-1453).
1485 - Richard III of England was defeated and killed at The Battle of Bosworth Field, the last of the Wars of the Roses between the Houses of Lancaster and York.
1567 - The Duke of Alba, sent to re-establish Spanish authority in the Netherlands, instituted the Council of Troubles at the start of his tyrannical rule. It was nicknamed the "Council of Blood".
1642 - The Civil War in England began, between the supporters of Charles I (Royalists or Cavaliers) and of Parliament (Roundheads).
1788 - The British settlement in Sierra Leone was founded. Britain said it was to provide a home in Africa for freed slaves and homeless Africans from England.
1818 - Warren Hastings, British administrator and first Governor-General of British India, died aged 85.

1834 - Samuel Pierpont Langley, U.S. astronomer and aviation pioneer, born. He specialised in studying solar effects on the weather and in 1896 built the first successful heavier-than-air flying machine.
1847 - Sir John Forrest, Australian explorer and politician, born. He led pioneer expeditions into Australia's western interior and was premier of Western Australia 1890-1901.
1851 - The U.S. yacht America outraced the British yacht Aurora off Cowes, England, winning the silver trophy offered by the Royal Yacht Squadron of Great Britain (America's Cup).
1862 - Claude Debussy, French composer known for such works as "Clair de lune" and "Prelude a l'Apres-midi d'un Faune", born.
1864 - The Geneva Convention for the protection of the wounded during times of active warfare was signed, leading to the formation of the Red Cross.
1893 - U.S. writer and satirist Doroth Parker was born. On the subject of suicide she wrote: "Guns aren't lawful; nooses give; gas smells awful; you might as well live".
1910 - Korea was annexed by Japan after five years as a protectorate.
1914 - Austria-Hungary declared war on Belgium.
1922 - Irish politician and Sinn Fein leader Michael Collins was killed in an ambush. He led the Irish delegation which signed the 1921 Anglo-Irish treaty by which Ireland was partioned.
1928 - German composer Karlheinz Stockhausen born. From 1953 he was foremost in the development of electronic music.
1930 - The two halves of Sydney Harbour Bridge were joined together. It was eventually opened in March 1932.
1941 - Nazi troops reached the outskirts of Leningrad. They eventually surrounded the city on September 8 at the start of the siege which lasted until January 1944.
1942 - Michel Fokine, Russian dancer and choreographer, died aged 62; he was a great influence on 20th century classical ballet.
1962 - The Savannah, the world's first nuclear-powered ship, completed her maiden voyage from Yorktown, Virginia, to Savannah, Georgia.
1968 - Pope Paul VI arrived in Colombia on the first visit by a pontiff to Latin America.
1971 - Bolivian President General Juan Jose Torres Gonzalez was deposed in a coup by Colonel Hugo Banzer Suarez, who drew support from the right-wing Falange Socialista Boliviana and the army.
1973 - Henry Kissinger was named U.S. Secretary of State, replacing William Rogers.
1978 - President Jomo Kenyatta of Kenya died in his 80s. His exact date of birth was never firmly established.
1978 - In Nicaragua, Sandinista guerrillas took over the National Palace for three days, killing six and taking several hundred hostages.
1985 - 55 people were killed at Manchester airport when a British Airtours Boeing 737 burst into flames after the pilot aborted the takeoff.
1994 - Jordan, overwhelmed by a flood of refugees, closed its border to arrivals from Kuwait and Iraq.
1995 - Parliament elected Negaso Gidada president of the newly-named Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.
1996 - The 61-nation Conference on Disarmament in Geneva ended in failure after India blocked an agreement on a Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.
